link_scope: Focused link reuses existing WTSTools and WTSUtils libraries from build-cov. This does not prove a clean rebuild or full aggregate integration.
root_cause: read_file_contents truncated the 64-bit file size to unsigned int, resized the caller output, then wrote through a cast from read-only std::string::c_str(), which is undefined behavior. A failed read could leave the caller buffer changed. The Windows read branches did not check ReadFile's BOOL result; the POSIX read_file_length path did not check a negative read before converting it to an unsigned value.
fix: Check ReadFile success and POSIX read errors; validate file size against size_t/string capacity and the Windows transfer limit; read into a temporary mutable string through &contents[0], then swap into the caller buffer only after a complete successful read.
acceptance: The macOS arm64 focused run passes all 14 BoostFile cases plus 12 IniHelper regression cases (26/26 total). It covers exact/short reads, closed-handle failures, binary round-trip, and preserving the caller buffer for missing/empty input. Independent review of the repaired source passed.
remaining: Windows native build and ReadFile failure execution were not run; the Windows branch is not platform-verified.
The focused link reused existing WTSTools/WTSUtils libraries; clean rebuild and complete aggregate/consumer integration remain unverified.
A successful read_file_length result larger than INT_MAX still narrows through its int return type; this existing size boundary remains outside the tested fix.
Other platforms and production callers remain unverified.
